name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
Information Systems – 2022/2023
Course Project
Consider the following scenario:

A km-zero fruit and vegetable store wants to develop a management system for am Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS; in Italian, Gruppo di Acquisti Solidale, or GAS) that connects a number of customers (family groups or generally groups of people) and some farmers. The basic philosophy is a conscious approach to purchasing, involving knowledge of the origin, quality, and different types of products.

The supporting information system should provide service to customers, farmers, and store employees.

The operating cycle of the EPS is weekly:
- Starting at 12 noon on Friday and by 9 a.m. on Saturday morning, farmers provide an estimate of available products, in terms of types, prices, and quantities,
- Customer orders are accepted until 11 p.m. on Sunday,
- By 9 a.m. on Monday morning the farmers confirm the availability of products,
- At this point the system automatically performs payments from customers' virtual wallets,
- After payment has been made, customers can schedule times to pick up produce,
- By Tuesday evening, farmers deliver their products to the store,
- Pickups can take place from Wednesday morning to Friday evening.

The information system has a catalog of products that describes the characteristics, contains photos, and indicates the unit of measurement with which they are sold (for example: €/kg). In addition, a minimum and a maximum quantity that can be ordered is indicated.

The availabilities entered by farmers refer to a product in the catalog, specify the total quantity available and a price (with the same unit of measure indicated in the catalog). It is also possible to indicate crop characteristics, e.g., small size, excellent quality, very ripe, etc.

Customers can choose from all the offerings of the various farmers by specifying the quantity and completing an order. The order can be placed directly by customers via the web or by store employees at the customers' request. Once the customer confirms the product entry, the system verifies that the minimum quantities are met: if not, the customer must modify the order before it can be finally confirmed. Once the order is completed, a summary email is sent to the customer.

Please note that the customer is a representative of a buying group, typically family groups or more generally groups of people. Therefore, only the group representative can enter group orders into the system.

Customer orders are in the "entered" state until the farmers confirm available quantities. If the available quantities are sufficient to cover the orders, the orders move to the "confirmed" status. If there is no availability for all orders of a certain product, according to the system's precedence rules, unavailable quantities are removed from lower precedence orders. Modified orders go into the "modified" status and must be viewed and accepted by customers. If all products in an order are unavailable, then the order is cancelled. Upon delivery of the farmers' products, the clerk confirms receipt of the products in the specified quantity. If by 4 p.m. on Tuesday the goods have still not been delivered the system sends a reminder via SMS. If at the end of the day (8 p.m.) the goods have not been delivered, the system changes the orders related to delivery, re-credits the amount of goods not present with a bonus of 20% and reports the inconvenience to customers.

Payment of orders is made after confirmation of quantities by farmers, for the quantities actually in the order. Payment is made from a personal wallet that users can top up at any time through the store.

After order placement, if the customer's wallet balance is insufficient, a warning is sent via email but the order is still accepted.

If the balance is insufficient at the time of payment, a message (SMS) is sent to the customer who has until Monday evening to top up their wallet. If the balance is not sufficient on Monday evening, the order is cancelled.

As soon as the payment is made (automatically by the system) customers can book an appointment to pick up their products at the store.

Store employees at the beginning of their shift view the pickup schedule and prepare packages for customers, when they arrive they register the pickup of products.

In case of failure to pick up on time, the system sends an SMS alert to the customer.

If the customer has not picked up their order by Friday, it is marked as "forfeited" and the customer's fair play score is updated as detailed in the following.

The system has a mean of evaluation the “fair play” of customers registered in the system. The customer’s fair play score is a measure of how correctly the users behave regarding their orders. This score is maintained in the system and is used as a mean of precedence in case of limited availability of produce. The “fair play” score is computed based on four different indicators: O) number of computed orders; R) number of reminders received; F) number of forfeited pickups; M) number of modified orders. When there is not enough availability of produce for all orders, the customers with higher score are given precedence over those with lower score.
highLevelGoals: Customers should be able to view the product catalog, select desired items, specify quantities, and place orders through the web interface or with employee assistance.
Customers need to manage their virtual wallet, top it up, and have payments for confirmed orders automatically processed.
Customers must be able to book specific time slots for picking up their confirmed and paid orders at the store.
Customers need to receive timely notifications and updates regarding their order status, including confirmations, modifications, or cancellations.
Customers expect a fair system for product allocation based on their 'fair play' score when product availability is limited.
Farmers need to provide and update estimates of available products, including types, quantities, and prices, within the specified weekly cycle.
Farmers must be able to confirm the actual availability of products to fulfill customer orders.
Farmers need a clear process for delivering their products to the store by the specified deadline.
Store employees need to maintain an up-to-date catalog of products with descriptions, photos, units of measurement, and quantity limits.
Store employees should be able to place orders on behalf of customers who request assistance.
Store employees must be able to confirm the quantity of products received from farmers and manage any discrepancies.
Store employees need to view the pickup schedule, prepare customer packages, and register when customers pick up their orders.
lowLevelGoals: Customers should be able to call an API to get a list of all products currently available in the catalog, including their descriptions, photos, units of measurement, and current prices.
Customers should be able to call an API to add a particular product to their shopping cart, specifying the desired quantity.
Customers should be able to call an API to modify the quantity of an already added product in their shopping cart.
Customers should be able to call an API to remove a specific product from their shopping cart.
Customers should be able to call an API to finalize their shopping cart and place a new order.
The system should automatically verify that all products in a submitted order meet their minimum quantity requirements before confirming the order.
Customers should be able to call an API to check the current balance of their virtual wallet.
Customers should be able to call an API to add funds to their virtual wallet, specifying the amount.
The system should automatically call an internal API to deduct the order total from the customer's virtual wallet upon order confirmation.
The system should automatically re-credit the customer's virtual wallet with a 20% bonus if products are not delivered by 8 PM on Tuesday.
The system should automatically send an email warning to the customer if their virtual wallet balance is insufficient at the time of order placement.
The system should automatically send an SMS to the customer to top up their virtual wallet by Monday evening if the balance is insufficient at payment time.
Customers should be able to call an API to view a list of available time slots for order pickup.
Customers should be able to call an API to reserve a specific time slot for picking up their order.
Customers should be able to call an API to change the previously booked pickup time for an order.
Customers should be able to call an API to cancel a previously booked pickup time for an order.
The system should automatically update a customer's 'fair play' score when a scheduled pickup is forfeited.
The system should automatically send an SMS alert to the customer if a scheduled pickup fails.
Customers should be able to call an API to get real-time updates on the status of their order (e.g., 'pending', 'confirmed', 'ready for pickup', 'picked up').
The system should automatically send a notification (e.g., email, push notification) to the customer when their order status is updated.
The system should automatically send a notification to the customer upon successful confirmation of their order.
The system should automatically send a notification to the customer if their order is modified by a store employee or due to product availability.
Customers should be able to call an API to accept or reject modifications made to their order.
The system should automatically send a notification to the customer if their order is cancelled.
The system should automatically report the inconvenience to customers if goods are not delivered by 8 PM on Tuesday.
Customers should be able to call an API to view their current 'fair play' score, which influences product allocation.
The system should automatically call an internal API to allocate limited products to customers, prioritizing those with higher 'fair play' scores.
The system should automatically update a customer's 'fair play' score based on the number of orders placed.
The system should automatically update a customer's 'fair play' score based on the number of reminders received.
The system should automatically update a customer's 'fair play' score based on the number of modified orders.

Farmers should be able to call an API to provide their estimated product availability, including product type, quantity, price, and crop characteristics (e.g., small size, excellent quality), for the upcoming weekly cycle.
Farmers should be able to call an API to modify their previously submitted product availability estimates, including crop characteristics.
Farmers should be able to call an API to confirm the exact quantities of products they can supply to fulfill customer orders.
Farmers should be able to call an API to view a list of customer orders that require their product delivery to the store.
The system should automatically send an SMS reminder to farmers if goods are not delivered by 4 PM on Tuesday.
Store employees should be able to call an API to add a new product, including its description, photo, unit of measurement, and quantity limits, to the system's catalog.
Store employees should be able to call an API to modify the description, photo, unit of measurement, or quantity limits of an existing product.
Store employees should be able to call an API to delete a product from the system's catalog.
Store employees should be able to call an API to create and submit an order for a specific customer, selecting products and quantities.
Store employees should be able to call an API to verify and record the actual quantity of products delivered by a farmer against the expected quantity.
Store employees should be able to call an API to log any differences between the expected and received quantities of products from a farmer.
Store employees should be able to call an API to view a list of all scheduled customer pickups for a given day.
Store employees should be able to call an API to indicate that a specific customer's order package is ready for pickup.
Store employees should be able to call an API to record that a customer has successfully picked up their order.
Store employees should be able to call an API to manage the status of forfeited pickups, including marking them as such.
